value.rationale: Metric discordance for a canonical bipartite root-polytope deletion is motivated by stability of polytopal geometry under sparse vertex/edge removal. The theorem quantifies three geometrically different notions (relative volume, worst-case Hausdorff, random-angle width) and yields exact rare-direction probability and a genuinely nontrivial conditional distribution, not a cosmetic substitution or a tabular recomputation. The width result goes beyond known volume and combinatorial data.
